sentences.zh: 迈克一提及营地，就有几个人打退堂鼓了，但至少有十几位潜在买家秘密来到老车站查看房产。

sentences.en: Most of the time, they don't call back, Mike said.
sentences.zh: 迈克说，大多数时候，他们不会回电。

sentences.en: If I track them down, it's like,
sentences.zh: 如果我追过去问，就像是，

sentences.en: God bless those people for staying in business, because I couldn't do it.
sentences.zh: 上帝保佑那些能坚持经营下去的人，因为我做不到。

sentences.en: It's taken years off my life,
sentences.zh: 这让我的寿命缩短了好几年，

sentences.en: Debbie said.
sentences.zh: 黛比说。

sentences.en: For her, it's, get me out, we've got to sell, sell, sell,
sentences.zh: 对她而言，就是：让我离开，我们必须卖掉、卖掉、卖掉，

sentences.en: Joe said.
sentences.zh: 乔说。

sentences.en: But we refused an offer for $250,000 eight years ago, and it keeps dropping.
sentences.zh: 但我们八年前拒绝了一份25.5万美元的报价，而且价格一直在跌。

sentences.en: I don't want to give this place away.
sentences.zh: 我不想白白送掉这个地方。

sentences.en: I can't afford it.
sentences.zh: 我承担不起。

sentences.en: I get it, said Mike.
sentences.zh: 迈克说，我懂。

sentences.en: If you were a half mile in another direction, you'd be sitting on a million bucks.
sentences.zh: 如果你往另一个方向走半英里，你就能坐拥百万美金了。

sentences.en: Instead, it's, how can you dispose of it?
sentences.zh: 相反，现在的问题是，你们怎么才能摆脱它？

sentences.en: Joe sat with that word for a moment as he smoothed the wrinkles from his apron.
sentences.zh: 乔一边抚平围裙上的褶皱，一边琢磨着这个词。

sentences.en: He had worked in restaurants since he was 15 when he started washing dishes at his father's Italian diner in Montreal.
sentences.zh: 他从15岁起就在餐馆工作，当时他在蒙特利尔他父亲的意大利餐馆洗盘子。

sentences.en: He'd learned how to cook and keep the books, but his father had mostly shown him that a restaurant could succeed because of an owner's charisma, and Joe brought that philosophy
sentences.zh: 他学会了如何做饭和记账，但他的父亲主要向他展示了一家餐厅之所以能成功是因为老板的个人魅力，而乔将这种哲学带到了

sentences.en: to Phoenix.
sentences.zh: 菲尼克斯。

sentences.en: A lot of places could make a good ham and cheese.
sentences.zh: 很多地方都能做出好吃的火腿奶酪三明治。

sentences.en: Old Station had thrived for 37 years because of Debbie's hugs at the entryway,
sentences.zh: 老车站之所以能繁荣37年，是因为黛比在门口的拥抱、

sentences.en: Joe's teasing at the register, and the hand-picked signs and inside jokes that covered every inch of their walls.
sentences.zh: 乔在收银台的调侃，以及覆盖了他们墙壁每一寸的精选招牌和内部笑话。

sentences.en: We've put all of ourselves into this place,
sentences.zh: 我们把全部心血都投入到了这个地方，

sentences.en: Joe said.
sentences.zh: 乔说。

sentences.en: They didn't have a pension.
sentences.zh: 他们没有养老金。

sentences.en: Their plan had always been to invest in the business, sell it, and use that money to retire.
sentences.zh: 他们的计划一直是投资这项生意，将其卖掉，然后用这笔钱退休。

sentences.en: They weren't seeking any damages in their lawsuit, but instead were asking the city to remove the encampment and find a different solution to care for its occupants.
sentences.zh: 他们在诉讼中不寻求任何损害赔偿，而是要求市政府拆除营地，并寻找不同的解决方案来照顾里面的居民。

sentences.en: Lawyers for the city had argued in court that the case should be dismissed because Phoenix was already working to go, quote, above and beyond to address the problem.
sentences.zh: 市政府的律师在法庭上辩称，此案应予驳回，因为菲尼克斯已经在努力采取引述，超越常规的措施来解决这个问题。

sentences.en: It had opened a new office of homeless solutions, and it was spending more than $50 million on outreach programs, mental health services, and the creation of 800 more shelter beds
sentences.zh: 它开设了一个新的无家可归者解决方案办公室，并斥资5000多万美元用于外展计划、心理健康服务以及在

sentences.en: in converted hotels and refurbished shipping containers.
sentences.zh: 改建的酒店和翻新的集装箱中建造另外800张收容床位。

sentences.en: Maybe it all turns around in a few years,
sentences.zh: 也许几年后一切都会好转，

sentences.en: Joe said.
sentences.zh: 乔说。

sentences.en: That's not on my timeline,
sentences.zh: 这不在我的时间表内，

sentences.en: Debbie said.
sentences.zh: 黛比说。

sentences.en: Physically and mentally, I cannot keep waking up to this level of stress.
sentences.zh: 在身体和精神上，我无法继续承受这种程度的压力。

sentences.en: But maybe in six months,
sentences.zh: 但也许在六个月内，

sentences.en: Joe started, and she shook her head and gestured across the street.
sentences.zh: 乔刚开口，她就摇了摇头，向街对面指了指。

sentences.en: You'll be dealing with this alone, she said.
sentences.zh: 她说，你得独自面对这一切了。

sentences.en: It's aging you.
sentences.zh: 这让你日渐衰老。

sentences.en: It's eating you up.
sentences.zh: 这在把你生吞活剥。

sentences.en: How much longer can you do it?
sentences.zh: 你还能坚持多久？

sentences.en: I don't know, he said.
sentences.zh: 他说，我不知道。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收看《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was
sentences.zh: 甚至在我还是

sentences.en: DJing in nightclubs, in the era of vinyl, every night, you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth into this, like,
sentences.zh: 在夜总会打碟的黑胶唱片时代，每天晚上，你都要带着300张最珍贵的藏品去上班，把DJ台变成一个，就像是，

sentences.en: living pop-up museum of beautiful
sentences.zh: 充满美丽且

sentences.en: 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 50年历史文物的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 立即在您最喜欢的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: A few days later,
sentences.zh: 几天后，

sentences.en: Joe drove four blocks through the encampment to visit the one person who could always make him feel better about the state of the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 乔开车穿过四个街区的营地，去拜访那个总是能让他对这个社区现状感觉好一些的人。

sentences.en: Joel Copland,
sentences.zh: 乔尔·科普兰，

sentences.en: 68, owned a building that was now surrounded by more than 55 tents, and yet he continued to run an art gallery downstairs and live with his wife upstairs.
sentences.zh: 68岁，拥有一栋现在被55顶以上帐篷包围的建筑，然而他依然坚持在楼下经营一家艺术画廊，并和妻子住在楼上。

sentences.en: He never seemed to run out of hope or compassion or patience, and that's what Joe thought he needed.
sentences.zh: 他似乎永远有着用不完的希望、同情和耐心，而这正是乔自认为需要的。

sentences.en: Meet the luckiest dog in the world,
sentences.zh: 来见见世界上最幸运的狗，

sentences.en: Joel said to Joe, introducing him to a stray puppy that he'd adopted after its owner overdosed in the encampment.
sentences.zh: 乔尔对乔说，向他介绍了一只流浪小狗，它的主人在营地吸毒过量后，他收养了它。

sentences.en: She'd been tied up and barking for days when I found her.
sentences.zh: 我发现它的时候，它已经被绑着叫了好几天了。

sentences.en: You've got a good heart, buddy,
sentences.zh: 伙计，你有一颗善良的心，

sentences.en: Joe said.
sentences.zh: 乔说。

sentences.en: Me, maybe not so much anymore.
sentences.zh: 我嘛，可能没那么善良了。

sentences.en: I've got a bleeding heart,
sentences.zh: 我这人就是心太软，

sentences.en: Joel said, inviting him inside.
sentences.zh: 乔尔说着，把对方请进了屋。

sentences.en: The gallery had been named the best new art space in Phoenix when it opened in 2019, but lately Joel could barely persuade a dozen people to come into the neighborhood
sentences.zh: 这家画廊在2019年开业时曾被评为菲尼克斯最好的新艺术空间，但最近乔尔几乎说服不了十几个人来到这个街区

sentences.en: for a weekend opening, so he decided to turn his attention to the bigger problems outside.
sentences.zh: 参加周末的开幕活动，于是他决定将注意力转向外面更严重的问题。

sentences.en: He'd lived for a while in an abandoned building in Hell's Kitchen when he was an art student in New York, and he knew what it was like to be homeless.
sentences.zh: 他在纽约读艺术院校时，曾在地狱厨房的一栋废弃建筑里住过一段时间，他知道无家可归是什么滋味。

sentences.en: He began inviting some of his neighbors into the gallery, offering them food and firewood, paying for some of their medical bills, and sometimes painting
sentences.zh: 他开始邀请一些邻居进入画廊，为他们提供食物和柴火，帮他们支付部分医疗费用，有时还给他们画画

sentences.en: He had tried to help Sterling, who sang prayers in Apache over his meals at the soup kitchen and lived for a while in the bed of Joel's truck, and Rosie, a grandmother
sentences.zh: 他曾试图帮助斯特林，斯特林在救济站吃饭时用阿帕奇语唱着祈祷曲，并在乔尔的卡车后斗里住过一段时间；还有罗西，一个祖母

sentences.en: and a heroin addict who was always asking
sentences.zh: 同时也是个海洛因瘾君子，总是向

sentences.en: Joel for, quote, one last five, which he kept giving to her, and Jennifer, a prostitute in the encampment whom he allowed to use his bathroom until she started bringing guests
sentences.zh: 乔尔要所谓“最后五块钱”，而他也一直给她；还有詹妮弗，营地里的一名妓女，他允许她使用自己的洗手间，直到她开始带客人

sentences.en: with her.
sentences.zh: 一起来。

sentences.en: He banned her from the restroom despite her pleading, and a few nights later she was arrested a block away for public urination.
sentences.zh: 尽管她百般哀求，他还是禁止她使用洗手间，几天后，她在隔壁街区因随地小便而被捕。

sentences.en: That charge triggered a warrant for another previous offense, which meant she was now serving four years in prison, and Joel was putting
sentences.zh: 这项指控触发了对她之前另一项罪行的逮捕令，这意味着她现在要在监狱里服刑四年，而乔尔则往

sentences.en: $80 each month onto her commissary card to help assuage his guilt.
sentences.zh: 她的狱中账户里每月存入80美元，以减轻自己的内疚感。

sentences.en: And then there was Keisha, barely out of her teens, who had skittered around the encampment like a scared cat, wary of everyone, carrying a few old dolls and crying sometimes.
sentences.zh: 还有基莎，刚刚脱离十几岁的年纪，像一只受惊的猫一样在营地里惊慌失措地四处乱窜，对所有人都充满戒备，手里拿着几个旧娃娃，有时还会哭泣。

sentences.en: Joel had tried to watch out for her, offering her water or a few minutes inside whenever she was upset.
sentences.zh: 乔尔一直试图照看她，每当她心烦意乱时，就给她提供水或让她进屋待几分钟。

sentences.en: But one weekend, when he wasn't around, the temperature was 115 degrees, and she laid down on the curb near his gallery and died of heat exposure and dehydration.
sentences.zh: 但某个周末，当他不在的时候，气温高达115华氏度，她倒在画廊附近的路边，因中暑和脱水而死。

sentences.en: Not a lot of happy endings here these days,
sentences.zh: 这年头，这里可没什么皆大欢喜的结局，

sentences.en: Joel said.
sentences.zh: 乔尔说。

sentences.en: He took out his phone, handed it to Joe, and hit play on a video that he had recorded a few nights earlier from the window of his upstairs apartment.
sentences.zh: 他掏出手机递给乔，并点开了一段视频，那是他几天前从楼上公寓的窗户里录下来的。

sentences.en: There were 26 broken streetlights in the encampment because of vandalism and wire theft, so the video was dark except for the reflection of police lights, which illuminated
sentences.zh: 营地里有26盏路灯因遭蓄意破坏和盗割电线而损坏，因此视频一片漆黑，只有警灯的反光照亮了

sentences.en: one man being handcuffed and another lying dead on the ground.
sentences.zh: 一个人被戴上手铐，另一个人倒地身亡的场景。

sentences.en: My wife and I were relaxing after dinner, all fat and happy, and then it was bap, bap, bap, bap, bap,
sentences.zh: 我和妻子晚饭后正在放松，吃得饱饱的、心情大好，然后就是砰、砰、砰、砰、砰的枪声，

sentences.en: Joel said.
sentences.zh: 乔尔说。

sentences.en: Did you hit the floor,
sentences.zh: 你们趴到地上了吗，

sentences.en: Joe asked?
sentences.zh: 乔问？

sentences.en: Well, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，倒地了。

sentences.en: We have our castle dark and our fortress strong, but it's becoming crazy.
sentences.zh: 我们的城堡虽然漆黑，堡垒虽然坚固，但这一切正变得越来越疯狂。

sentences.en: Our fence got cut the other night and there was a woman in our yard, screaming and yelling her head off in Spanish.
sentences.zh: 前几天我们的栅栏被剪断了，院子里有个女人用西班牙语歇斯底里地大喊大叫。

sentences.en: Joe handed back the phone and shook his head.
sentences.zh: 乔把手机还了回去，摇了摇头。

sentences.en: I'm realizing here lately that we're living in a frigging hellhole, he said.
sentences.zh: 我最近意识到我们正生活在一个该死的人间地狱里，他说。

sentences.en: Us, them, inside, outside.
sentences.zh: 我们，他们，里面，外面。

sentences.en: Who's it working for?
sentences.zh: 这到底对谁有用？

sentences.en: When does it stop?
sentences.zh: 这什么时候才是个头？

sentences.en: Not yet, Joel said.
sentences.zh: 还没呢，乔尔说。

sentences.en: He explained that he had heard rumors from within the encampment that there would be more gunfire because of a turf battle over pieces of the sidewalk.
sentences.zh: 他解释说，他从营地内部听到传言，由于争夺人行道地盘的帮派冲突，将会有更多的枪击事件。

sentences.en: Joel had already called to warn the police and now he suggested that Joe leave the neighborhood before dark.
sentences.zh: 乔尔已经打电话警告了警察，现在他建议乔在天黑前离开这个街区。

sentences.en: It's hard to believe, but they're telling me it will get worse, he said.
sentences.zh: 真令人难以置信，但他们告诉我情况还会恶化，他说。

sentences.en: Joe arrived for work early the next morning to the sound of a gunshot coming from across the street and a bullet pinging off a nearby fence.
sentences.zh: 第二天一大早，乔来到店里上班，伴随着一声从街对面传来的枪响，一颗子弹击中了附近的一处栅栏并发出了叮当声。

sentences.en: He hurried inside the restaurant and locked the door behind him.
sentences.zh: 他快步走进餐厅，反锁上了身后的门。

sentences.en: He crouched low beneath the windows and called the police.
sentences.zh: 他压低身子蹲在窗户下面，报了警。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's Joe again over at Old Station, he said, and a few minutes later two police officers were walking the perimeter of his restaurant with flashlights in the predawn darkness
sentences.zh: 喂，我是老车站餐厅的乔，他又打通了电话，几分钟后，两名警察在黎明前的黑暗中拿着手电筒沿着他的餐厅外围巡视

sentences.en: searching for the bullet.
sentences.zh: 寻找子弹。

sentences.en: Joe ran cold water over his hands, changed into his apron, and tried to focus on the day ahead.
sentences.zh: 乔用冷水冲了冲手，换上围裙，试图把注意力集中在即将开始的一天上。

sentences.en: Fresh fruit cup on special, he wrote on the chalkboard, and then he started preparing fruit cups as he looked outside and watched the encampment stir to life as if it were just
sentences.zh: 今日特供鲜果杯，他在黑板上写道，然后开始准备水果杯，同时向外看去，看着营地如往常一样

sentences.en: any other morning.
sentences.zh: 充满生机地苏醒过来。

sentences.en: Espy set up her desk on the corner.
sentences.zh: 埃斯皮在角落里摆好了桌子。

sentences.en: Kip came out of his tent and started assembling his window washing pole.
sentences.zh: 基普从帐篷里出来，开始组装他的擦窗杆。

sentences.en: The police drove through the area and left without making any arrests.
sentences.zh: 警察开车巡视了该地区，没有逮捕任何人就离开了。

sentences.en: KD came out of his tent with his pit bull and started pacing the sidewalk, screaming to himself, waving his arms in the air, and narrating the events of the previous night
sentences.zh: KD带着他的比特犬从帐篷里出来，开始在人行道上踱步，自言自语地尖叫，双手在空中挥舞，向所有人

sentences.en: for everyone to hear.
sentences.zh: 讲述着前一晚发生的事情。

sentences.en: Y'all made me go psychotic, psychotic, he yelled as Joe stirred his tomato sauce.
sentences.zh: 你们把我逼成精神病了，精神病，乔尔搅拌着番茄酱时，他大喊道。

sentences.en: You come at me with a nine millimeter and I'm pulling out my 45, KD said as Joe weighed the turkey.
sentences.zh: 你们拿九毫米手枪来找我，那我就掏出我的四五口径手枪，乔在称火鸡肉时，KD说道。

sentences.en: Next time, there won't be no warning shot,
sentences.zh: 下次可就没有警告射击了，

sentences.en: KD shouted as Joe unlocked the door for the first customer of the morning and looked up at the clock.
sentences.zh: KD大喊着，与此同时，乔为早上的第一位顾客打开了门，抬头看了一眼时钟。

sentences.en: It was just after 8 a.m.
sentences.zh: 刚过早上8点。

sentences.en: By now, Debbie would be waking up and getting ready for work.
sentences.zh: 这会儿，黛比应该已经醒来并准备去上班了。

sentences.en: Soon, she would be pulling into the parking lot to help handle the lunch rush.
sentences.zh: 不久，她就会把车开进停车场，帮忙应付午餐高峰。

sentences.en: What the heck am I going to tell her to keep her from losing it,
sentences.zh: 我到底该怎么跟她说，才能让她不至于崩溃，

sentences.en: Joe wondered as he began to rehearse the possibilities in his head.
sentences.zh: 乔在脑海中反复排练着各种可能的话语时，心里琢磨着。

sentences.en: It was only one bullet.
sentences.zh: 这只是一颗子弹。

sentences.en: Nobody had gotten hurt.
sentences.zh: 没有人受伤。

sentences.en: The police had come right away.
sentences.zh: 警察立刻就来了。

sentences.en: The shooter wasn't targeting the restaurant.
sentences.zh: 开枪的人不是冲着餐厅来的。

sentences.en: The gunshot was random.
sentences.zh: 枪声是随机的。

sentences.en: It could have happened anywhere.
sentences.zh: 这种事在哪儿都可能发生。

sentences.en: Joe poured tomato sauce over the meatballs and went outside to get some air.
sentences.zh: 乔把番茄酱浇在肉丸上，走到外面去透透气。

sentences.en: KD was still ranting on the sidewalk, banging his hand against a fence, contorting his fingers into the shape of a gun and then firing it off at the sky.
sentences.zh: KD还在人行道上叫骂，用手猛击栅栏，把手指扭成枪的形状，然后朝天空开枪。

sentences.en: This could be the last straw for her,
sentences.zh: 对她来说，这可能是压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草，

sentences.en: Joe said.
sentences.zh: 乔心想。

sentences.en: And then he saw Debbie driving toward the parking lot, steering around KD and hurrying through the gate.
sentences.zh: 就在这时，他看见黛比开车驶向停车场，绕过KD，匆忙穿过大门。

sentences.en: Wow, tough morning, she asked.
